body:
Founder direction, citing Hyperbot's own event-driven architecture: 'ensure we are doing event driven instead of polling.' Found and fixed a real, live CPU-wasting bug: --fast-forward's socket is O_NONBLOCK, so the main loop free-spun as fast as CPU allowed even with zero new packets, ticking/broadcasting continuously regardless of real state change -- live-measured earlier this session at ~100% CPU on an idle server, flooding idle clients' sockets (S446's own regression test had to explicitly service both sides every tick to avoid it). Fixed by blocking on select() with a bounded 10ms ceiling (so wall-clock matchmaking timeouts still fire) instead of a non-blocking recvfrom() in a tight loop -- scoped to --fast-forward only, real-time mode's own usleep(16000) pacing is unchanged. Live-verified: idle CPU now ~0.0-0.1% (was ~100%), zero added latency when clients are actively sending. Real self-destruct tick timing is now accurate again (251 real ticks, not the previously stale-input-inflated ~50-90 apparent ticks) -- the permanent regression test's own tick budget was corrected to match. Full C build + 72/72 Python tests pass. Commit 9bcabda.

⚓ ☃
title: S450: event-driven server main loop replaces --fast-forward busy-spin
